notes: Finding 1 is grounded: E-005 documents roughly $672B of fee-bearing capital and AUM above $1T, E-053 documents Q2/H1 2026 fundraising, and C-009 correctly prevents treating AUM or commitments as currently fee-earning economics.

Finding 2 is grounded: E-015 documents more than $5B of BWS deployment into Brookfield-originated assets, E-016 documents affiliate investment-management fees, and C-013 correctly preserves the related-party elimination/double-count issue.
Finding 3 is directionally grounded by E-036, E-037 and E-038, which show large-scale alternative-asset-management capability outside Brookfield.

However, E-039 and E-042 are incorrectly placed in counterevidence_ids. E-039 explicitly supplies another scaled peer-platform example, and E-042 documents Brookfield participating alongside several large competing capital providers. Both reinforce replicability/competition rather than counter it.
Because counterevidence field semantics are part of the human-quality contract, the observation is not comparison-admissible despite schemaValid=true and semanticValid=true.
No post-hoc repair or retry is authorized.

cross_role_luna_observation.interpretation: Brookfield shows that engineering semantic validation is necessary but not sufficient: evidence IDs may be canonical while their analytical role is misclassified. No model winner or routing rule is frozen.
